name: nut-puller
title: Joint rig: nut puller
orientation: Flat on the bed, either face down: one plain plate. One screw through it into the slot nut under test
description: A tab screwed to one slot nut in the joint rig's base beam, with a hole at its end for a luggage scale's hook: pull along the slot until the nut slips, and read the scale. Its screw hole takes M5 and smaller; the plate is sized so the screw's shank bearing on it holds about twice a 50 kg luggage scale's top reading (load_margin, an M4 the smallest screw). MEASURE.md, row 37.

wide.rule: As wide as the beam's 20 mm face

long.rule: Along the slot: the screw near one end, the hook's hole near the other

thick.rule: 6.4 mm: what the smallest screw's shank bearing on the plate needs to hold about twice the scale's top reading (load_margin), and the thickness at which a sold M5x12 button screw engages a slot nut fully and stops short of the slot's floor

hook.rule: The hole for the scale's hook or a loop of cord

screw_x.rule: The screw, a face's width in from the far end: over the slot nut

hook_x.rule: The hook's hole, at the end the scale pulls toward

edge.rule: Plastic past the hook's hole, which the hook would tear out

round.rule: The plate's corners, rounded so they stay down

pull.rule: The most a common luggage scale reads, 50 kg, at 9.81 N/kg: the pull the tab is sized for

shank.rule: The smallest screw the slot nuts under test take, M4: its shank bears on the plate hardest

bearing.rule: The pressure of the screw's shank on the plate at the scale's top reading

tear.rule: The stress beside the hook's hole at the scale's top reading

shear.rule: The shear on the two planes the hook would tear out along

load_margin.value: min(pla.strength / bearing, pla.strength / tear, pla.strength * 0.577 / shear)
load_margin.rule: The weakest way the tab fails, over PLA's strength (shear at 0.577 of it, one over the square root of 3, von Mises; bearing taken at the strength itself, on the safe side): the kit asks about twice
